long_biography.plain_text:
Rothberg founded CuraGen while completing his Yale doctorate, combining biology, engineering and computation in one of the early genomics companies. He then created 454 Life Sciences to commercialize massively parallel DNA sequencing. CuraGen sold that subsidiary to Roche, while Rothberg later founded Ion Torrent and retained stronger founder voting control before Life Technologies acquired it. Those acquisition prices valued company equity, not disclosed personal proceeds; corporate owners and outside investors also participated.

He subsequently built 4Catalyzer to launch several ventures in parallel. Its companies apply semiconductors, artificial intelligence and life-science research to portable ultrasound, point-of-care magnetic-resonance imaging, protein sequencing, diagnostics and therapeutics. Rothberg remains the incubator's founder and chairman, serves on the boards of Butterfly Network, Quantum-Si and Hyperfine, and retains disclosed voting power in those public companies. Their market capitalizations and the private ecosystem's funding totals are company-level measures, not his net worth. Likewise, foundation resources and laboratory equipment belong to the relevant nonprofit or operating entity rather than to Rothberg personally.

uncertainties.detail: Yale and Carnegie Mellon independently establish 1963 and New Haven but do not give a day or month. The existing exact Wikipedia profile gives 28 April, while the National Medal site shows a conflicting January date. Day and month remain review-only below the 85-point threshold.

Rothberg separately founded the companies that created his principal wealth and is not classified as inheriting them. His father's successful engineering company, entrepreneurial upbringing and early commercial exposure support an advantaged start, although no source establishes that family capital financed CuraGen.
454 was a majority-owned CuraGen subsidiary when Roche acquired it. CuraGen recorded the corporate gain, so the acquisition value is not presented as Rothberg's personal sale proceeds.

Life Technologies paid cash and stock for all outstanding equity and offered milestone consideration to sellers. Rothberg retained enhanced voting control before the sale, but his exact economic ownership and net personal proceeds are not disclosed in the cited sources.

SEC beneficial-ownership figures can include direct shares, trusts, affiliated entities and holdings for which Rothberg disclaims economic ownership. The dossier describes disclosed voting and board interests without treating each reported share or an entire company valuation as his personal asset.

4Catalyzer's private companies have raised outside capital. Funding totals and private-company valuations measure corporate financing or investor pricing, not Rothberg's net worth, and no private venture is assumed to be wholly owned by him.

Resources held by a charitable foundation, university, research program, incubator or operating company remain assets of that entity. Scientific use or founder association does not make equipment, grants, laboratories or budgets Rothberg's personal property.
